reason: The kidney blood sample is approaching the filter shown in the nephron preparation, so this directly starts the filtering goal.
expectation: The nephron should filter some fluid and dissolved substances from the blood.

effect: The filter lets fluid and small substances into the tubule while retaining blood cells and most proteins. Next I should try recovering useful substances.
reaction: It was helpful to see what stays in the blood.
reason: The selective transporters are in the tubule wall next to blood, so they look suited to returning useful dissolved substances.
expectation: Some useful dissolved substances will move from the tubule back toward the blood.

effect: The transporters returned glucose and other useful substances toward the blood. The remaining sample can now be used to follow water recovery.
reaction: It was useful to see that the kidney normally recovers almost all filtered glucose.
reason: The water-permeable tubule picture shows water moving toward blood, matching the next recovery step.
expectation: Some water will move from the tubule back toward the blood.

effect: Water returned to the blood while wastes remained in the tubule. The remaining sample can follow the urinary drainage route.
reaction: The picture makes the separation clear.
reason: Urinary drainage leads from the kidney toward the bladder, so it is the next route for the remaining fluid.
expectation: The remaining fluid will pass into the urinary drainage route as urine.

effect: The remaining fluid became urine moving through a ureter to the bladder, completing the filtering goal. I can now connect the urinary organs to the body.
reaction: The path from filtering to the bladder is clear.
reason: The kidney pair has a named ureter slot, and the ureters lead toward the bladder.
expectation: The ureters will attach to the kidneys.

effect: The ureters are attached to the kidneys; the bladder still needs to be fitted.
reaction: The named slot made that step straightforward.
reason: The bladder is the other named slot, and the ureters lead to it.
expectation: The bladder will attach to the kidney and ureter assembly.

effect: The bladder is fitted, completing the kidney-to-bladder route. I can now connect the urinary organs to the body.
reaction: The route is straightforward to follow.
reason: The remaining goal is to connect the urinary organs to the body, and the kidney assembly now has both named parts.
expectation: The urinary organs will connect to the body and its blood supply.

effect: The kidneys are now connected to the body's circulation, with ureters leading to the bladder. Both goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the filtering process connected to the whole body.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the filtered sample through recovery was most worthwhile: it showed that the kidneys return useful substances and water to the blood rather than simply removing waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the ureters and bladder was clear but less engaging because the named slots made the choices predictable.

surprise.text: I was surprised that healthy kidneys normally recover almost all the glucose that was filtered.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and named slots explained the route and the parts.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how another body system connects, though this chapter's straightforward assembly steps were less interesting than following the filtering process.
